answer: Charge each agent a verifiable-action fee settled in escrow: an agent must stake a bond before submitting work, and a sparrow-sized watcher pool randomly audits a fraction of outputs, slashing the bond on mismatch. Since the audit draw is keyed by a per-identity cipher hash, attackers can't predict which fake identities get checked, so each extra sybil account adds fresh bond plus expected-slash cost. Honest agents recover their stake and earn nectar rewards from the slashed pool, making mass-identity farming more expensive than the marginal reward per verified action.
